developer: Forus, Inc. (formerly Tandem / Tandem Technology, Inc.), based in New York, NY.
regulatoryApprovalStatus: Not an FDA-authorized medical device; administrative medication-access / prior-authorization workflow platform (consumer/provider tooling).
availability: Free for providers and patients in the United States; supports practices in all 50 states and works with any EHR.
summary: Forus is an AI-powered medication access platform that automates steps from prescription to affordable treatment—prior authorizations, appeals, enrollment forms, benefit verifications, pharmacy routing, affordability programs, and patient communication—so patients can start therapy faster.
medicalPurpose: Accelerate and simplify patient access to prescribed medications by automating administrative medication-access workflows (including pharmacy-benefit and buy-and-bill support) across drugs, insurance plans, and pharmacies.
acceptableInput: Prescription and patient information from the clinician’s EHR workflow (prescribe in the EHR as usual; Forus generates and submits payer-specific prior authorization materials).
output: Automated prior authorizations, customized appeal letters, enrollment forms, pharmacy routing, benefit verifications, affordability/financial assistance options, and patient/provider status updates.
roleInDecisionMaking: Forus automates administrative work after the clinical decision to prescribe; it does not replace the clinician’s prescribing judgment. Clinicians prescribe the therapy they choose, and Forus handles access logistics.
intendedUsers: Clinicians and practice staff (including dermatology, allergy, GI, rheumatology, neurology, and other specialties), as well as pharmacies, payers, and biopharma partners connected through the Forus network.
targetPatientPopulation: U.S. patients prescribed medications that require prior authorization or other access support, including specialty and dermatology medications.
knownPerformanceLimitations: Forus focuses on medication access / prior authorization workflows; it is not a diagnostic or treatment-recommendation clinical AI. Practices that do not e-prescribe may have limited support. Performance can vary by payer, drug, and specialty. Specific model error rates are not publicly disclosed.
skinTypeRepresentationEquity: Not applicable to core administrative PA automation; skin-tone representation is not a product performance axis for Forus’s medication-access workflows.
requiredClinicianOversight: Yes. Clinicians remain responsible for the clinical decision to prescribe. Forus automates administrative medication-access steps after the prescription is placed.
modelType: AI-powered workflow automation / medication-access platform (including LLM-assisted PA form answering and appeal generation, with LLM-as-judge verification against patient records).

trainingData.description: Uses first-party prior authorization and medication-access interaction data from the platform network; detailed training corpora and foundation-model identities are not fully disclosed publicly.

modelDevelopmentAndValidation.description: Forus publishes engineering eval methods for its LLM judge (perturbation-based evaluation of PA answer verification against clinical records). Case studies on forus.com report practice-level access outcomes (e.g., Family Allergy & Asthma; DOCS Dermatology).

clinicalTrial.description: Not disclosed / not applicable as a drug or device pivotal trial for this administrative platform.

performance.summary: Provider-facing metrics reported by Forus include ~1.1 median days to prior authorization approval in featured practices, ~3× more authorizations completed per day, and ~2× greater success filling first-line prescriptions. Family Allergy & Asthma reported cutting PA turnaround from 7+ days to 1.1 days and ~70% lower per-patient admin workload; DOCS Dermatology reported same-day submissions with approvals in <1 day.

metrics.name: Median days to PA approval (featured practices)
Per-patient admin workload reduction (Family Allergy & Asthma)

performanceEvaluationLimitations: Public metrics are largely case studies / marketing outcomes rather than peer-reviewed diagnostic AUROC-style evaluations; independent validation is limited.
plansForOngoingMonitoring: Forus states it is HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, with end-to-end encryption and US-based enterprise storage; security documentation available via Trust Center / security@forus.com. Clinical Intelligence and engineering teams continuously improve PA automation and judge calibration.
scheduledUpdates: Continuous product iteration (not a fixed public release calendar).
